benchmark: Economic OS external object-centric event-log reference datasets

datasets.name: Procure-to-Pay (P2P)
datasets.role: Domain-level OCEL reference; tests multi-object lifecycle and known anomalies, not relational extraction from raw source DB.

datasets.name: Synthetic relational databases and reference OCELs

scenarios.pattern: in-table version history with valid/record time
SAP-style change documents and archive copies
bitemporal Data Vault and balanced asset journal

publisher_validation_claims: validation.json reports PASS for committed benchmark reports
source and canonical oracle SHA-256 digests checked against per-scenario validation report
SQLite integrity checks returned ok for copied source and generated OCEL databases
generated OCEL read back with matching PM4Py reader
event/object IDs and types, E2O/O2O relations, temporal change keys and row counts compared with canonical oracle
datasets.pinning_policy: Before a benchmark run, acquire the published SHA256SUMS and validation.json, pin every used file SHA-256 in a local run manifest, and verify checksums. Do not treat Zenodo record ID or MD5 shown on the landing page as a substitute for the package SHA-256 list.

matched_arms.name: Typed Mycelix OCEL

matched_arms.name: Full Economic OS projection
matched_arms.purpose: add owner-scoped causal sidecar, correction lineage and verifier knowledge frontier

guardrails: Published reference datasets are public development baselines, not hidden evaluation.
A parser-valid JSON file does not pass semantic reconstruction.
The candidate extractor cannot read the canonical reference OCEL or validation oracle in hidden evaluation.
No 100% event recall target where the canonical reference intentionally excludes technical rows; score justified inclusion/exclusion and explanation.
No performance score offsets a false economic assertion or silent semantic loss.
